title: Correcting the Naive Asymptotic of the Half-Integer Beta Diagonal
content: Establishes the large-n behaviour of the diagonal half-integer Euler Beta value: B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n). The parent entry's follow-up question conjectured the rate √(π/n); that is FALSE. The central binomial coefficient C(2n,n) grows only like 4^n, while the exact value B(n+1/2,n+1/2)=π·C(2n,n)/4^(2n) divides by 4^(2n); the surplus power leaves an exponentially decaying factor 4^(-n). So the Beta value vanishes geometrically, not at the polynomial rate n^(-1/2). The corrected rate matches the classical diagonal law B(x,x) ~ 2^(1-2x)·√(π/x) at x=n+1/2, where 2^(1-2x)=4^(-n).
prerequisites: the Beta function and its half-integer diagonal value
asymptotic equivalence f ~ g of sequences

title: Real Closed Form and the Beta-Integral Bridge
content: betaDiag n := π·C(2n,n)/4^(2n) repackages the parent's complex closed form as a real sequence, the object whose asymptotic is studied. betaIntegral_eq_betaDiag proves the complex Euler Beta integral Complex.betaIntegral (n+1/2) (n+1/2) equals (betaDiag n : ℂ) by rewriting with the parent's betaIntegral_diag_half_centralBinom and a push_cast/ring cleanup, so the asymptotic describes the genuine Beta value rather than an abstract sequence. betaDiag_pos records strict positivity from Nat.centralBinom_pos.

title: The Normalized Limit as a Pure Field Identity
content: betaDiag_normalized_tendsto proves B(n+1/2,n+1/2)·4^n·√(πn)/π → 1 by transporting StirlingFormulaOQ03OQ02.centralBinom_asymptotic (C(2n,n)·√(πn)/4^n → 1) along Filter.Tendsto.congr. The required pointwise identity C(2n,n)·√(πn)/4^n = betaDiag n·4^n·√(πn)/π is PURE FIELD ALGEBRA: after unfolding betaDiag and rewriting 4^(2n)=4^n·4^n, the π's cancel and the common factor √(πn) survives untouched, so field_simp closes it with no square-root reasoning at all. The normalizing factor 4^n·√(πn)/π is deliberately the exact reciprocal of the equivalent √(π/n)·4^(-n).

title: Upgrading to IsEquivalent and the Corrected Rate
content: betaDiag_isEquivalent states B(n+1/2,n+1/2) ~ √(π/n)·4^(-n) as an Asymptotics.IsEquivalent over atTop. The equivalent is eventually nonzero (n≥1), so isEquivalent_iff_tendsto_one reduces the claim to Tendsto (betaDiag n / (√(π/n)·4^(-n))) → 1, which equals the already-proven normalized limit once √(π/n) is rewritten as √(πn)/n (an identity proved with Real.sqrt_div, Real.sqrt_mul and Real.mul_self_sqrt) and a final (√(πn))²=πn step (Real.sq_sqrt). The surviving 4^(-n) in the equivalent is precisely the exponential factor the naive guess omitted; reading B(x,x)~2^(1-2x)√(π/x) at x=n+1/2 confirms it.
